title: Exploring Heterogeneity and Uncertainty for Graph-based Cognitive Diagnosis Models in Intelligent Education

problem.claim: Graph-based cognitive diagnosis models infer students' proficiency levels on knowledge concepts.

gap.claim: Existing graph-based cognitive diagnosis models neglect edge heterogeneity and uncertainty, preventing optimal performance.

contributions.claim: ISG-CD uses a semantic-aware graph neural network-based cognitive diagnosis model to utilize heterogeneous graphs.
ISG-CD introduces an Informative Edge Differentiation layer that learns a minimal yet sufficient reliable graph in an unsupervised way from an information bottleneck perspective.
ISG-CD optimizes the semantic-aware model and edge differentiation layer with mutual-information objectives, their stated loss-function realizations, and alternating training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrated the effectiveness of ISG-CD.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph-based cognitive diagnosis is used to infer student proficiency on knowledge concepts.
The models are described as limited by neglected edge heterogeneity and uncertainty, including ambiguity in correct and incorrect response logs.
ISG-CD combines semantic-aware graph neural networks with an informative edge differentiation layer.
The reliable-graph objective uses mutual information, binary cross entropy, HSIC, and alternating training.
Experiments on three real-world datasets are reported as demonstrating effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Response edges may differ in type and may have ambiguous semantic meanings.

interpretation.claim: Modeling edge heterogeneity and uncertainty may improve graph-based cognitive diagnosis.

application.claim: For graph-based educational prediction, distinguish response types and learn which edges are sufficiently reliable for diagnosis.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this approach improves performance across settings beyond the reported datasets.
